Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

School & learning

odd adjective

of a number: not divisible by two

also odd number, odd numbers, odds and evens, even number

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.32 (Lewis & Short): stēllārum numerus pār an impar sit, nescītur
Verg. E. 8.75 (Lewis & Short): numerō deus impare gaudet

impar, imparis

adjective, third declension, one ending; ablative singular imparī

odd (of a number); unequal

The opposite of pār, even: numerus pār, numerus impar. It also means unequal, no match for: impar esse + dative, “be unable to cope with” (Traupman 150; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • stēllārum numerus pār an impar sit, nescītur

    nobody knows whether the number of the stars is even or oddCic. Ac. 2.32 (Lewis & Short)

  • lūdere pār impar

    to play odds and evensHor. S. 2.3.248 (Lewis & Short, s.v. pār)

See also number, count, arithmetic, strange.

SourcesLewis & Short: impar · Lewis & Short: par

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 150, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
